title: Paired-View Sensitivity and Threshold Transfer in Frozen Vision Encoders for Fracture Detection
content: Background: A second view can change which fractures a model detects. We quantified this change and the transfer of a GRAZ threshold across cohorts. Methods: We trained frozen-encoder classifiers on 3,917 GRAZPEDWRI-DX examinations (7,834 radiographs). At GRAZ-derived thresholds we compared paired- and single-view sensitivity in 1,052 fracture-positive PediURF cases (DINOv2-504, SKELEX-224), and scored DINOv2-224 and SKELEX-224 on 491 MFXR patient-ID groups, 85 OrthoFrac-XR images, and 425 BoneFract Wrist images. Results: Adding the lateral (LAT) view to anteroposterior (AP) input raised sensitivity by 2.66 percentage points (pp; 95% CI +1.62 to +3.80) for DINOv2-504 and 0.38 pp (−0.29 to +1.05) for SKELEX-224; adding AP to LAT raised it by 1.62 pp (+0.86 to +2.47) and 4.37 pp (+3.14 to +5.70). Paired input missed five DINOv2-504 and four SKELEX-224 cases found by single views. In MFXR, the area under the curve (AUROC) was 0.599, 0.803, and 0.754 for DINOv2-224, SKELEX-224 and their average; the average reached 0.705 in OrthoFrac-XR and 0.711 in BoneFract, with specificity 2.9% and 6.5% at the GRAZ threshold (sensitivity 100% and 98.0%). Conclusions: The change depended on the model and starting projection. The fixed average showed moderate discrimination but classified most controls as positive at the GRAZ threshold.
